> Non-occupancy charges shall be levied at 50% of the prevailing maintenance charges per sq. ft. for units that remain unoccupied for a continuous period exceeding three months. **Subject: Amendment to Bye-Law No. 12 – Non-Occupancy Charges**

The managing committee, at its meeting held on 27-07-2024, resolved to amend Bye-Law No. 12 relating to non-occupancy charges. The amendment was necessitated by the increasing number of units remaining vacant for extended periods, leading to higher common-area maintenance costs per occupied unit.

The amended Bye-Law No. 12 shall read as follows:

> Non-occupancy charges shall be levied at 50% of the prevailing maintenance charges per sq. ft. for units that remain unoccupied for a continuous period exceeding three months. The charges shall be applicable from the first day of the fourth month of vacancy and shall be billed quarterly in arrears. Units under renovation, with prior intimation to the managing committee, shall be exempt for a maximum period of six months.

The amendment was approved by the managing committee with a majority of 7 out of 9 members. The amendment shall come into effect from 01-09-2024. All members were informed by circular dated 30-07-2024.

The amendment was necessitated by the increasing number of residents opting for electric vehicles and the consequent need for charging infrastructure.

The amended bye-law provides that any member desirous of installing a private charging point in their allotted parking space shall make a written application to the Secretary. | 12 | Contingency reserve (5% of total receipts) | 1,42,250 |
| 13 | Sinking fund contribution | 1,50,000 |
| 14 | Miscellaneous | 35,000 |

The total estimated expenditure for the year works out to ₹24,65,250, leaving an estimated surplus of ₹3,79,750, which the Finance Committee proposes to transfer to the General Reserve.

Mr. Prakash Nair sought clarification on the sinking fund contribution, noting that the previous year’s budget had provided only ₹1,00,000. Mr. S. V. Kulkarni explained that the increase was in line with the Society’s policy of building a corpus for the proposed re-laying of the internal roads, expected to be undertaken in 2024-25. The Chairperson noted that the increase had been discussed at the last Annual General Meeting and was reflected in the minutes of that meeting.

**Motion No. M-2023-001**

Moved by: Mr. S. V. Kulkarni
Seconded by: Mr. Sunil Pawar

*“RESOLVED that the Annual Budget for the Financial Year 2022-2023, as circulated and presented, showing total income of ₹28,45,000 and total expenditure of ₹24,65,250, be and is hereby approved.”*

Vote: For – 7, Against – 0, Abstain – 0

RESOLVED accordingly.

**Action:** The Treasurer to upload the approved budget on the Society’s member portal by 20th January 2023.

**Item No. 6: Appointment of Statutory Auditors for the Financial Year 2022-2023**

Chitnis & Associates, Chartered Accountants, would conclude with the audit of the accounts for the year ended 31st March 2022. The audit report for that year was received on 12th December 2022 and was tabled before the Committee.

The Chairperson placed on record the Committee’s appreciation for the prompt completion of the audit. The audit report for the year ended 31st March 2022 has been noted and filed. The financial statements for that year are now closed.
